summary: Climate shifts and water scarcity are threatening traditional farming calendars, leading to widespread crop failures. To address this, we developed Vinland, a satellite-powered web application that translates complex Earth observations into immediate, actionable agricultural intelligence. Vinland connects directly to the NASA POWER Agroclimatology (AG) API, fetching 14-day rolling telemetry including temperature extrema, root-zone soil wetness, and precipitation. By running these variables through an agronomic threshold engine across 21 global crops, Vinland delivers instant binary crop suitability diagnostics ("Suitable" vs. "High Risk"). If a field faces environmental stress such as unseasonal frost or drought, the system dynamically recommends viable substitute crops and outlines 12-to-24-month regenerative rotation pathways. By transforming raw satellite telemetry into an intuitive, pre-planting decision dashboard, Vinland empowers farmers worldwide to mitigate climate risk, conserve water, and protect yields.
details: This is Jericho, it's a web based engine that helps farmers pick their next crop rotations and adapt to the changes goin on around the world. It is gonna help farmers know if their farms/land is suitable for growing certain crops and if not or if there are any better crops suitable for that land based on the NASA data , its gonna tell them, along side recommend 3 plans for the rotation : standard, water conservation and soil regeneration. Vindland is programmed using Python, making use of commands like import requests to pull the NASA data, import pandas to help organise the pulled data so its easier to do maths on, as well as the streamlit library to help bring it online. The parameters that we put into consideration were : T2M(temp at 2 meters) - GWETROOT(soil moisture at root level) - T2M_MIN - T2M_MAX - RH2M(humidity at 2m) - WS2M (wind speed at 2m). We also let the farmaer choose seasons to tailor the plans to their needs.
